source.description:
## PROBLEM

Every read command (rank/compare/recommend) and the refresh command need a shared, testable data layer: types for the OpenRouter benchmark shape, a fetch function, and a TTL-cached read/write pair. Without a single module, each command would re-implement cache I/O and drift from the injectable-DI pattern this repo already uses for exactly this kind of thing.

## SUCCESS

A module exports: (1) a TypeScript type for one cached benchmark record and the on-disk cache shape (with fetchedAt), (2) defaultCacheFile() returning ~/.xtrm/cache/model-benchmarks.json, (3) a fetchBenchmarks(apiKey) function calling GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/benchmarks with the Bearer token, (4) readCache/writeCache mirroring npm-latest.ts's best-effort-swallow semantics, (5) a refreshBenchmarks(opts) orchestration function taking injectable {cacheFile, now, fetchFn, apiKey} exactly like npm-latest.ts's CheckOptions, so tests never touch the network.

## SCOPE

New file cli/src/utils/model-benchmarks.ts (same directory as cli/src/utils/npm-latest.ts, mirror its shape). Do not touch cli/src/utils/npm-latest.ts itself except to read it as a reference.

## NON_GOALS

- No CLI wiring (commander commands) — that's the refresh/rank/compare/recommend tasks.
- No retry/backoff logic beyond a single fetch attempt with a clear error on non-2xx — YAGNI until proven necessary.
- No caching of partial/error responses.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Mirror cli/src/utils/npm-latest.ts:27-45 (CheckOptions shape, defaultCacheFile, readCache/writeCache try/catch-swallow pattern) and :112-164 (orchestration function signature/DI shape) as closely as the different data makes sense.
- Use Node's built-in global `fetch` — no new dependency.
- Read OPENROUTER_API_KEY from process.env; if absent, fetchBenchmarks must throw/return a clear typed error rather than making an unauthenticated request. Never log the key value anywhere (console, thrown error message, cache file).
- The actual JSON field names returned by GET /api/v1/benchmarks are UNVERIFIED — this task must make one real call (locally, using a personal OPENROUTER_API_KEY, NOT committed anywhere) during implementation to confirm the response shape before finalizing the TypeScript type, then note the confirmed shape in the PR description / bead notes for downstream tasks (rank/compare/recommend) to rely on. If a real key isn't available at implementation time, model the type on the user's stated assumption (model_permaslug, agentic_index, coding_index, intelligence_index, pricing.prompt, pricing.completion) and flag the assumption explicitly rather than silently guessing further fields.
- Cache write failures must never throw out of refreshBenchmarks (same best-effort semantics as npm-latest.ts:59-66).

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit tests inject cacheFile (tmp path via mkdtempSync), now (fixed clock), and fetchFn (fake) — no real HTTP call in tests, no HTTP-mocking library, mirroring cli/src/tests/npm-latest.test.ts's DI style exactly.
- [ ] Test: cold cache (file absent) → refreshBenchmarks calls fetchFn and writes cache.
- [ ] Test: fresh cache (within TTL) → does NOT call fetchFn (unless a --no-cache-equivalent force flag is passed at the orchestration layer, matching npm-latest.ts's noCache option shape).
- [ ] Test: fetchFn throwing/rejecting → cache is left untouched, function surfaces a clear error, does not write garbage.
- [ ] Test: missing OPENROUTER_API_KEY → clear typed error, no network call attempted.
- [ ] `npm run build` and targeted `npm test --workspace cli -- model-benchmarks` green.

## LIBRARIES

- **Reuse in repo:** cli/src/utils/npm-latest.ts (path.join/os.homedir cache path convention, CheckOptions DI shape, readCache/writeCache swallow pattern) — direct structural template, cite in the module's top comment if useful.
- **Installed deps:** none needed.
- **Stdlib:** Node global `fetch` (Node 18+, already the runtime baseline per npm-latest.ts having no HTTP client dep); node:fs/node:path/node:os per npm-latest.ts's existing imports.
- **New dep candidate:** none — tiers 1-3 covered it.
- **Roll it:** yes — this is a small, single-purpose module with no existing package that fits (OpenRouter has no official JS SDK for this endpoint).

## OUTPUT

Changed files (model-benchmarks.ts + its test file), confirmed real API response field names (or explicit note that they remain assumed pending a live key), test output showing all DI-based unit tests passing.
source.title: Benchmark cache module — OpenRouter fetch + TTL cache + types
